items.text: “Some of you got to it. Some of you didn’t. Both are fine — ‘we didn’t get to it’ is honest, and honest is what we do here.”
One sentence about what it was like — “not what was said — that’s yours — just what it was like”
An arranged parent starts; then it’s open, and optional
“The work is happening, whether or not we name it tonight.”
Same psalm as last week, on purpose — nothing new tonight; we’re completing the round
One idea, repeated: the opposite of being hidden is not being exposed — it is being seen and being safe at the same time
The parents practiced that last Wednesday. Tonight the teens do
Put the comparison down — “Every story is its own. … The story you tell tonight is not in competition with any story told in this building last week. Tell yours.”

panel.label: PSALM 139:23–24
lines: “Search me, O God, and know my heart! Try me and know my thoughts! And see if there be any grievous way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting!”

items.text: “It’s one question — tell the story of how you got here, and what has shaped you.” The depth is yours to choose
“When you’re listening — don’t fix, don’t advise, don’t relate back. Receive, and after each story, bless.”
“Nothing leaves your cluster. Not a phrase, not a name, not a story.”
Same clusters and same rooms as last week — your family stays with you

slides.title: Stories in Family Clusters — the Teens Tell

items.text: The teens tell — same clusters, same single question, same blessing. Second running
Story — 5–7 minutes. Nobody interrupts, even the silences
Silence — ten seconds
Blessing round — the arranged parent blesses first, then the circle: one or two sentences each
Parents tonight: receive and bless — no correcting the record, no filling silences
“What’s said in this circle stays in this circle. And when someone is telling, we’re looking at them. We’re receiving.”
What happened in your cluster stays in your cluster
One word, when you’re ready, about what tonight was like — an arranged parent starts. You can pass
“The round is complete — every person in this room, parent and teen, has now told a piece of their story to a circle that blessed them for it.”
“Rooms like this one are rare. They’re also the kind of room God shows up in.”
Joint Footprints — for every family that hasn’t done it yet. Parent and teen, twenty minutes, sometime this week
Not in the car, not in front of a screen. Phones away
Five minutes telling, a follow-up question or two, and one sentence: “What I love about your footprints is...” Then swap
“Families who already did it — you’re done; don’t force a repeat.”
Everyone keeps the morning question and the evening journal note going — five minutes in the morning, two at night
